messages:
nick: Quick perf pass comparing init vs step kernel routing (init == prefill, step == decode). Ran on rtx-a100-prod-sim. Workload: mixed prefill+streaming, seq_len=64, step small-batches (1-4). Seeing ~18% p99 tail increase on the step path when FlashPaged kernel gets picked for step. Repro and short logs below.

nick: Repro command: ```./bench --model m --mode mixed --seq 64 --init-batch 8 --step-batch 2 --routing-config routing_v3.yaml --log-kernel-selection```

sofia: Can you paste the kernel selection snippet + kv stats from that run? :eyes:

nick: Kernel selection excerpt: ```[KERNEL_SELECT] seq=64 path=init chosen=flash_paged_v2 reason=high_throughput
[KERNEL_SELECT] seq=64 path=step chosen=flash_paged_v2 reason=latency_estimate
[KVCACHE] hits=12423 misses=2412 evictions=512 pages_in=768 pages_out=760```

alyssa: Hmm, both init and step picked flash_paged_v2. For small-batch decode we usually prefer flash_fused_small to avoid page thrash. Wondering if the heuristic token_threshold was bumped accidentally.

thomas: Which config controls that? IIRC step uses 'small_batch_token_threshold' and we default to 32 for step but routing_v3.yaml might set it globally to 256.

nick: Confirmed: routing_v3.yaml had `small_batch_token_threshold: 256` under the global section. That makes the estimate think step has enough tokens to justify paged. That explains the p99 spike.

sofia: Also KV numbers show evictions ~= pages_out -> page thrash when interleaving prefill writes and step reads. flash_paged is heavy on page table churn for small steps.

alyssa: Short-term mitigation: add a guard that forces fused attention for path==step && batch_size<=4. I'll prototype a flag `--force-step-fused`. Longer term: rework threshold logic to be path-aware (init vs step) and incorporate empirical kv_eviction cost.

nick: Quick run with `--force-step-fused` results: p99 step tail 153ms -> 128ms (-16.3%), overall throughput -4%. Logs: ```perf: step_p99_before=153ms after=128ms throughput_before=1200tok/s after=1152tok/s```

perf-bot: perf-run 1902345678-1: baseline -> failing p99 regression detected (+14% on step path). perf-run 1902345678-2 (with force-step-fused): p99 restored, throughput small drop. See raw csv at https://perf-board.internal/1902345678/csv

sofia: We should also add counters in runtime: kv_page_hits, kv_page_evictions_per_second, kv_prefill_writer_bytes. That will let us automatically trigger fused for hot eviction patterns.

alyssa: Agreed. I'll add instrumentation and an emergency fallback rule: if evictions/sec > 50 and path==step, prefer fused_small.

thomas: Can you open a PR with the flag + instrumentation + a perf test? Add a microbenchmark that interleaves 8 init requests with 16 step requests at small batch sizes to reproduce thrash deterministically.

nick: Will do. PR branch `runtime/step-fused-guard`. Attaching minimal flamegraph screenshot to the PR.

sofia: One more note: double-check quantization kernels; we had a variant where quantized flash_paged was much slower on short sequences due to extra unpack cost. Might amplify this.

alyssa: Good call. I'll include a quantized path check in the heuristic.

thomas: Assigning follow-up to alyssa. Also add an automated canary in dedicated that flips `small_batch_token_threshold` between 32 and 256 for 1h to catch regressions early.

nick: OK, opening PR and adding perf job. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: created perf alert `step_tail_flashpaged_regression` -> notify #eng-runtime if p99 > 140ms for 5m

nick: Closing loop: PR link in 10m, will tag reviewers @sofia @alyssa.
